mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in housing starts by more than 10% over two months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST declined by more than 10% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over three consecutive months signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased employment supports consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it signals strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending drives economic growth.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher rates and inflation erode corporate profits.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% month-over-month, it signals a significant economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic weakness spreads.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 consecutive quarters and HOUST declines > 5% month-over-month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 was negative for two consecutive quarters and HOUST declined by more than 5% month-over-month.
